Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the USA's reply! The two Umpires are already out to the middle and out walk the two USA openers Steven Taylor and the skipper, Monank Patel. Pakistan players take their respective fielding positions with Shaheen Afridi warming up before getting the proceedings underway with the new ball with two slips in place. And, here we go.
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Right then, the USA may have restricted Pakistan on an average score but they will have to chase it down, and it surely won't be a cakewalk for them. They will have to battle it out against the fiery Pakistani pace battery to get their second victory. Pakistan will aim to reap the benefits from the surface and get those early breakthroughs to push their opponents on the back foot from the get-go. Stick around and stay tuned as the chase is up next in just a few moments.

Nosthush Kenjige is in for a flash interview. He says that they are pretty pleased to restrict Pakistan to 159 but feels that it is still half the job done. Shares that it is a very good wicket and they are looking forward to the chase. Adds that they know that Pakistan are a strong side but they believe in their abilities. Tells that they would have taken this target before the start of the game. Hopes that the team can bat well to get over the line.

The USA seamers were sharp, maintaining tight lines and lengths, giving no room to the batters. The ball moved around a lot, and the bowlers took full advantage of the assistance from the surface. Saurabh Netravalkar dismissed Rizwan with a beauty, thanks to a stunning catch from Steven Taylor. Nosthush Kenjige and Ali Khan also chipped in with wickets in quick succession. Although Pakistan managed to score quickly around the halfway mark and were hinting towards a big score, Nosthush Kenjige's double whammy brought success back to the USA. Jessy Singh then dismissed Babar Azam and compounded the pressure further. With these three wickets in quick intervals, all the USA needed was a stronger finish in the death overs and they exactly did the needful. Saurabh Netravalkar closed up well and ended with tremendous figures with a couple of wickets, conceding just 18 runs. As a result, the USA gave away just 46 in the last five overs.

An incredible bowling performance from the USA through and through as they restrict Pakistan to a below-par score. Pakistan were sent in to bat first and immediately found themselves in trouble, looking unsettled from the start. Mohammad Rizwan managed to hit a six, but couldn't add any more. Usman Khan fell while attempting an unnecessary shot, and Fakhar Zaman hit a couple of boundaries before being undone by extra bounce and pace. Pakistan crawled through the Powerplay, losing three key wickets cheaply. Babar Azam fought through the first six overs cautiously. He then partnered with Shadab Khan, and together they put on a resilient 72-run partnership, with Shadab being the real aggressor, scoring a quickfire 40 before getting out. This allowed Babar to settle in, and he eventually hit some quick boundaries before being dismissed for 44. Just when Pakistan seemed to have gotten the momentum back, those three quick wickets again stemmed the flow of runs to an extent. And with Iftikhar Ahmed's departure after a sedate cameo and Shaheen Afridi providing those final touches, it helped Pakistan to go past 150.

Yes, he can. Just a single to end the Pakistan innings. Nails the yorker tailing back in, on middle and leg, Shaheen Afridi can only squeeze it out to long on for a run. 10 runs off the last over take Pakistan to 159.

Commentary.Commentary: Done with the national anthems and we are all set to go. Blue skies greet the two umpires as they shake hands and make their way out to the centre. Monank Patel and his men stride out to the middle and they get greeted with a loud cheer from the USA fans. It will be the experienced duo of Babar Azam and Mohammad Rizwan to open the innings for Pakistan. The USA are starting with spin in the form of Nosthush Kenjige. The countdown is done and dusted. Away we go...

We are moments away from getting underway, but before that, the match officials and the two sets of players will line up for the national anthems. It will be Pakistan's first, followed by the national anthem of the USA.

Naseem Shah is in for a chat. He says his body has recovered well, and the preparation has been good. Considering the last two games played at his venue, he reckons that the wicket has been good. Feels that the first game of any tournament is important for the momentum, and they aim to start well. States that they have a strong bowling attack, but bowling in partnerships will be the key.

Babar Azam, the skipper of Pakistan says they would have bowled first as well since it is a morning game. Says it's a good surface and looks fresh. Also says it's good to see the sunshine which was missing since a few days. Adds that they will look to bat well in the Powerplay. Informs Imad Wasim is missing due to an injury, and they are going with four seamers.

The captain of the USA, Monank Patel says that they will bowl first. Tells that the reason behind electing to bowl first is that they have played before on this surface and chasing has been easier at this venue. Also says that they want to know what they are chasing. Shares that they have the momentum from the game against Canada and want to continue. States that they are looking forward to his game and that they are excited about this new challenge. Informs that they have made one change with Nosthush Kenjige coming in for Shadley van Schalkwyk.

USA (Playing XI) - Steven Taylor, Monank Patel (C/WK), Andries Gous, Aaron Jones, Nitish Kumar, Corey Anderson, Harmeet Singh, Jessy Singh, Nosthush Kenjige (In for Shadley van Schalkwyk), Saurabh Netravalkar, Ali Khan.
Pakistan (Playing XI) - Babar Azam (C), Mohammad Rizwan (WK), Usman Khan, Fakhar Zaman, Azam Khan, Iftikhar Ahmed, Shadab Khan, Shaheen Afridi, Naseem Shah, Mohammad Amir, Haris Rauf.
TOSS UPDATE - Monank Patel, the skipper of USA wins the coin-flip and elects to BOWL first.

Pakistan, on the other hand, is entering this World Cup following a series defeat against England and a humbling loss during their Irish tour. They haven't been living up to their strengths recently. Further compounding their worries, crafty spinner Imad Wasim is injured and won't participate, making Shadab Khan's experience on these spin-friendly drop-in pitches crucial. Their pace battery, featuring speedsters like Shaheen Afridi, Naseem Shah, and Haris Rauf, needs to translate their abilities into performance. On the batting front, Mohammad Rizwan and Babar Azam have been the only consistent performers, while Fakhar Zaman and Iftikhar Ahmed are expected to play aggressive clutch roles more frequently. With Pakistan as the heavyweights, will they maintain their reputation, or does the USA have more surprises in store? Stay tuned as the toss and teams are up next.

The USA has exceeded expectations, making a strong mark in their brief crickeing history with their impressive performances recently. The hosts are brimming with confidence, having won four out of their last five matches along with a series win against Bangladesh. Starting their league phase with a victory against Canada, the USA have shown they can't be underestimated at all. However, this time, their challenge elevates to a new level as they face Pakistan. Aaron Jones has been simply sensational with the bat, showcasing his wide array of strokes and ability to take down the spinners with his range-hitting prowess and will be the crucial X-factor. Andries Gous too, looks in fine form and these two along with likes of Steven Taylor and Corey Anderson would play key roles with the bat and ball. While the bowling unit needs some obvious improvements, USA lineup surely packs a serious punch.
